prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1470; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received after a low-speed head-on collision. The insured's vehicle sustained front-end damage, and the claimant, who is represented by counsel, reported neck pain and stiffness shortly after the incident. The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the parties and the physical evidence.

Entry 3: Scene and vehicle photos were obtained and show damage that matches the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the medical summary. The claimant's account of how the collision happened has remained the same in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Medical records reviewed. The diagnosed injury is consistent with the kind and force of a collision of this type. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Records also show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years. That earlier condition may contribute to some of the current complaints, and the file notes this for evaluation.

Entry 7: Current status: liability and injury review are in progress, with the prior treatment history and the attorney's demand package still under consideration. Next step is to request the complete prior records before setting a reserve.
